s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain over the clavicular area with a tender mass and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain over the left clavicular area
Tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with erythema
Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on chest radiograph
key_facts: No fever, weight loss, or trauma
Tender swelling over the left clavicle
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
Normal complete blood count, renal and liver function tests
Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on chest radiograph

raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on the chest radiograph, along with an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and a tender swelling over the left clavicle, is most consistent with Ewing's sarcoma, a malignant bone tumor that can cause such radiographic and clinical findings.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis typically presents with signs of infection such as fever, discharge, and elevated white blood cell count, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: While Langerhans cell histiocytosis can cause lytic bone lesions, it often involves multiple sites and can have systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are typically benign and may not cause systemic symptoms like an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by recurrent episodes of osteomyelitis, often with a more complex and prolonged course than described in the vignette.
